solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sleazy bar outside City area is influential

indicators.note: one thing standing outside another wraps around it, so the outer piece splits to enclose the rest

parts.note: a dive is a seedy, disreputable drinking place
EC is the postcode area covering the City of London
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seedy bar on the edge of the financial district turns out to have real sway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link before the definition, but it goes inside with EC; the City is London's financial district, whose postcode letters are EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decisive settles an outcome, so it carries real weight and sway over what happens.

clue.text: Avoid Italian magistrate imprisoning daughter

indicators.note: to imprison is to hold someone inside, so one piece holds another within it

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone wants to steer clear of a Venetian official who has locked up his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The doge was the elected ruler of the old Venetian republic; D goes between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to evade or sidestep something, such as a question or a falling object.

clue.text: I initially avoid clubs after what could be ace of hearts

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it, so the later words go at the end

parts.note: an ace is one example of a playing card
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: first letter of avoid
first letter of clubs

explanation.surface: A card player tries to avoid playing clubs, having an ace of hearts in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ace of hearts' reads as one card, but the clue splits it: 'what could be ace' is the card and 'of hearts' is the definition. 'I' stands alone, unshortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac is the medical adjective relating to the heart, as in cardiac arrest.

clue.text: Puts on tense fight like a starry-eyed player?

parts.note: to stage a play is to put it on
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a ruck is a scuffle or brawl

explanation.surface: A dreamy young actor dresses for a tense brawl on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts on' sounds like dressing, but here it means putting on a show; a ruck is also the rugby term for a loose scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dazzled by the theatre and longing to act is said to be enchanted by its glamour, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Reportedly in France, you perform black magic

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the spoken form matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: vous is French for you, and to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that you practise the dark arts while living in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' marks the French word for you, vous, which is pronounced like the first syllable; add the English verb do.
explanation.definitionFit: Voodoo is a Caribbean religion popularly associated with spells and curses, so it serves as a byword for sorcery.

clue.text: Suddenly realise what grows on tree

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal verb for catching on or understanding
second meaning: a small shoot from a branch

explanation.walkthrough: The informal sense of catching on is chiefly British slang, as in 'I finally twigged what she meant'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a slangy verb for grasping something at last and a noun for a slender woody shoot.

clue.text: Buzz initially within hive is running riot

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so each following word gives just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Inside a beehive the humming swells as the colony runs wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz initially' tempts you to take the B, but 'initially' governs the words after it, and 'Buzz' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirr is a continuous vibrating hum, the kind of steady noise wings or machinery make.

clue.text: Escape, breaking gate system

indicators.note: something broken falls apart and can be put back in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
a way of doing something is a method or system

explanation.surface: A prisoner gets out by smashing through the gate mechanism.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the four letters of the gate are rearranged; 'system' stays whole as a synonym added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway is a fleeing act, typically after a crime, so the noun matches a flight from captivity.

clue.text: Skin expert got old-timer as transformed

indicators.note: a transformed thing has been changed in form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A skin specialist sees an elderly patient whose complexion has been rejuvenated.
explanation.walkthrough: All thirteen letters of the three middle words are used exactly once.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical specialist diagnoses and treats conditions of the epidermis, hair and nails.

clue.text: No longer being obstructive? That's unusual

definitions.meaning: first meaning: moved aside so as not to block anything
second meaning: remote or out of the ordinary

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks whether something has stepped aside; the second meaning describes places off the beaten track or quirky things.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means cleared from someone's path, and figuratively means remote or uncommon.

clue.text: Best one of those scoring one in Scrabble turns?

indicators.note: something that turns faces the other way, so the letters read backwards

parts.words: one of those scoring one in Scrabble
parts.note: the E tile is worth one point in Scrabble

explanation.surface: A question about which of the one-point tiles is top in a game of Scrabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' looks like players' turns in the game, but it signals the reversal; Scrabble pieces are tiles, and E scores one point.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the pick of a group, the top tier, so it stands for 'the best' as a collective noun.

clue.text: Get too big for old hat having good line

parts.note: something old hat is out of fashion
G is the abbreviation for good
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A head grows too large for a battered old hat with a nice trim line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' reads as a garment, but it is the idiom for unfashionable, which gives OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Children outgrow clothes and shoes when they become too large to fit them.

clue.text: Spur incorporated it by end of shoe

parts.note: Inc. is the abbreviation for incorporated, used after company names
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of shoe

explanation.surface: A rider's spur is fastened at the heel of a boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spur' reads as the rider's spiked heel fitting, which suits the shoe, but it is the verb meaning urge on.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on is to goad or provoke them into action, the same as inciting them.

clue.text: Drunk, perhaps, I am investing billions in German beer

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: to invest is to put money into something, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: Bier is the German word for beer
B is the abbreviation for billions

explanation.surface: A tipsy speaker boasts of sinking a fortune into the German brewing trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as an adjective, but here it is a noun, a person who drinks too much; 'perhaps' warns that this is one example of a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbiber is someone who drinks alcohol, and a drunk is an extreme example of such a person.

clue.text: Brawl with a very loud fellow

parts.note: taken as written
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
Ray is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A punch-up breaks out involving a particularly noisy man.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a 'fellow' or 'man' can be any short male name; here it is Ray.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public fight that frightens bystanders, also a legal term for such disorder.

clue.text: Partly secret sin — alcoholic drink

indicators.note: partly means only in part, so a portion of the following words is taken

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A confession that one's hidden vice is booze.
explanation.walkthrough: The A comes from 'alcoholic', which also reads naturally with 'drink' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, so it is a type of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Part of threat on a link having no established key

indicators.note: a part of something is a portion of it, so a stretch of the following words is taken

parts.note: letters running across the four words

explanation.surface: Someone threatens to break into a website link lacking a security key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests locks and passwords, but it is the musical sense of a home pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music avoids any tonal centre, so it is not written in a recognisable major or minor scale.

clue.text: Flowers I dropped in heaving boutique

indicators.note: heaving means surging and churning, so the letters are thrown into a new order
something dropped is let go and left out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written, the letter to remove
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lets a bunch of flowers fall in a packed, bustling shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heaving' is British slang for very crowded, which fits the shop; remove the I from the shop word and rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet is an arranged bunch of blooms, so plural 'Flowers' describes it as a collective noun.

clue.text: Employment of university philosopher

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
a sage is a wise thinker

explanation.surface: A philosopher has a job at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employment' suggests a job, but here it means putting something to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage and employment both name the act of using or applying something, as with tools or words.

clue.text: Where one can stay very warm — the middle of Hell

parts.note: very warm is hot

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central part, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of Hell

explanation.surface: Deep in Hell is a place where you can keep nicely toasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Hell has four letters, so its middle is the two letters between the H and the final L.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel offers rooms for travellers, so it is a place providing paid lodging overnight.

clue.text: Belgian city under feudal tenure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a major city in eastern Belgium
second meaning: bound to give or receive feudal service

explanation.walkthrough: The city is spelt with an accent in French, Liège; the adjective describes vassals and lords in the medieval feudal system.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Walloon city and also describes the bond of loyalty between a vassal and lord.

clue.text: Both sides on board admitting no middle ground

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the two opposing players in chess or draughts
second meaning: seeing things as simply right or wrong

explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' sounds like being in agreement, but it is a game board; the two sides in chess are named after their colours.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the two chess armies and also describes absolute thinking that ignores grey areas or nuance.

clue.text: Victor leaves noisy celebration dance

indicators.note: when someone leaves they go away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a revel is a lively, noisy party
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The winner walks out of a rowdy party where everyone is dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a winner, but it is the radio code word for V.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance, so it is one kind of dance.

clue.text: Make winning chess move for childhood friend

parts.note: to make a move in a game is to play it
checkmate, shortened to mate, wins a chess game

explanation.surface: A child beats an old friend at chess.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the phrase literally tells you to deliver the deciding chess move, and the two words that do so join up.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a companion a child plays games with, so it is a friend from early years.
